name: Familial Episodic Pain Syndrome with Predominantly Upper Body Involvement
aliases: Familial Episodic Upper Body Pain Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Proposed Diagnostic Criteria for Familial Episodic Pain Syndrome with Upper Body Involvement

criteria.description: Recurrent episodes of severe, paroxysmal pain predominantly affecting the upper body regions including neck, shoulders, and arms
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance pattern
Neurological examination is normal between pain episodes
Laboratory tests show absence of systemic inflammation during episodes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of recurrent upper body episodic pain with a positive family history; supportive findings strengthen diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing may assist but is not mandatory for diagnosis

pathognomonic.symptomName: Paroxysmal severe upper limb and shoulder pain
pathognomonic.notes: Pain episodes last from minutes to hours
searchTerms: sudden severe arm and shoulder pain

pathognomonic.symptomName: Familial clustering of episodic pain attacks

common.symptomName: Transient neck stiffness during pain episodes
Autonomic symptoms including flushing and sweating localized to upper body
common.notes: Considered part of neurological autonomic involvement

searchTerms: transient pins and needles in arms

occasional.symptomName: Occasional nausea during severe pain attacks

rare.symptomName: Transient mild tachycardia during pain episodes
Mild localized skin erythema over affected areas
searchTerms: mild skin flushing over pain area

laboratory: Normal inflammatory markers (CRP, ESR) during and between episodes
imaging: Normal MRI and X-rays of cervical spine and upper limbs

distinguishingFeatures: Pain predominantly in distal extremities with marked redness and warmth
Triggered by heat and relieved by cooling
Progressive sensory loss and autonomic dysfunction

redFlags: Systemic signs of inflammation or infection
Unexplained weight loss or constitutional symptoms
references: Orphanet: Familial Episodic Pain Syndrome with Predominantly Upper Body Involvement, ORPHA:391389
